::: {.why}
You will be asked what you conclude when the two disagree, and the answer is not a coin flip; it is a statement about the power of each test at your sample length.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State both null hypotheses precisely and say what you conclude in each of the four possible outcome combinations.
- Report the power of the ADF test against a stationary alternative with an autoregressive root of 0.98 at your sample length.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>55 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Run both tests on five series: an index level, its returns, a yield, a spread and one of your simulated random walks. Tabulate the four possible outcomes and write the conclusion for each combination, including the case where both reject and the case where neither does.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Measure the power, which is the part textbooks omit: simulate AR(1) series with coefficients of 0.9, 0.95, 0.98 and 0.99 at 500 and 2,000 observations, and report the fraction of times ADF rejects the unit root. The result at 0.98 with 500 observations is the reason a failure to reject means very little.
:::
:::
